schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Restarts the app service and rotates its log directory.

    type: String
  LogPath:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '.*'
  DbPassword:
    type: SecureString

    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript

        commands:

    inputs:

      Script: |-
        import boto3

            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}

I'll keep the parameter but rename it, noting it's currently unused since nothing retrieves the password value, and provide the retrieval pattern as part of the proposed fix for when the restart logic is actually added. I should note that if real passwords were ever passed through executions, they'd show up in execution history as plaintext and should be rotated as a precaution. The LogPath pattern is too permissive — needs tightening to a critical-level fix. Every check\\nin this chapter is grounded in a public Systems Manager or IAM documentation page, cited in\\n[references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md](references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md).\\n\\nThis review is static. It reads the document only. It doesn\\'t run the runbook, and it doesn\\'t\\ncheck the IAM policy of the role the runbook assumes; review that role separately.\\n\\n## When to use\\n\\n- A user asks to review or harden a runbook they wrote, before publishing or sharing it.\\n- A release or prevention review includes account-owned runbooks.\\n\\nTo choose a runbook for a problem, hand off to\\n[references/automation/runbook-discovery.md](references/automation/runbook-discovery.md); to run one, to\\n[references/automation/execution.md](references/automation/execution.md).\\n\\n## Workflow\\n\\nCopy this checklist and work through it in order:\\n\\n- [ ] Step 1: Read the document (Phase 1)\\n- [ ] Step 2: Scan with every check in the detection rules (Phase 2)\\n- [ ] Step 3: Apply, propose or flag fixes (Phase 3)\\n- [ ] Step 4: Write the report and the hardened document (Phase 4)\\n- [ ] Step 5: Check the output, then present it\\n\\n## Phase 1: Read the document\\n\\n1. Get the document. If the user names a runbook in their account, call\\n   `aws ssm get-document --name <name> --region <region>`, and add `--document-version <n>` if\\n   they named a version. Otherwise use the content the user provides.\\n2. Note the format (YAML or JSON). The hardened document must use the same format.\\n3. Check `schemaVersion`. If it isn\\'t `\"0.3\"`, stop: Automation runbooks must use schema version\\n   0.3. A `2.2` document is a Command document, which this chapter doesn\\'t cover.\\n4. List `parameters` (name, type, constraints), `assumeRole`, and every step in `mainSteps`\\n   (name, action, inputs, `onFailure`, `onCancel`, `timeoutSeconds`, `maxAttempts`), including\\n   steps nested in `aws:loop`.\\n\\n## Phase 2: Scan\\n\\nOpen [references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md](references/automation/hardening-detection-rules.md) and apply every check, in\\norder:\\n\\n| # | Check | Severity |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| 1 | Command injection: parameters or step outputs interpolated into shell or PowerShell commands | Critical |\\n| 2 | Secrets: hard-coded credentials, secret values passed as parameters, secrets in outputs | Critical |\\n| 3 | Parameter validation: missing or weak `allowedPattern`, `allowedValues`, length and item limits | High (Critical for parameters used in commands) |\\n| 4 | Role: missing `assumeRole` where the runbook needs it | High |\\n| 5 | Step limits: timeouts beyond documented limits | Medium |\\n| 6 | Failure and cancel routing: invalid `onFailure` / `onCancel` values or targets | Medium |\\n| 7 | Approval steps: `aws:approve` misconfiguration | Medium |\\n| 8 | Cross-account role assumption from a step | Medium |\\n| 9 | TLS verification disabled in a command or script | High |\\n| 10 | Document structure: schema version, required fields, parameter types, step names | Low |\\n\\nFor each finding record the check number, severity, the parameter or step (and JSON path), what is\\nwrong, and the documentation page that backs it.\\n\\nNever repeat a secret\\'s value in a finding. Give its location and tell the user to rotate it.\\n\\n## Phase 3: Fix\\n\\nUse [references/automation/hardening-fix-patterns.md](references/automation/hardening-fix-patterns.md). Fixes come in three kinds:\\n\\n| Kind | Applies to | What you do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Apply | Deterministic changes to existing fields: add or tighten `allowedPattern`, fix an ARN pattern\\'s partition, correct a timeout above a documented maximum, correct an invalid parameter type | Change the document directly. Don\\'t add steps |\\n| Propose | Changes that alter behaviour: rewriting a command that interpolates parameters, moving a secret to Parameter Store, adding `assumeRole`, rerouting `onCancel` | Apply in the hardened document, and show each change as BEFORE / AFTER with the reason |\\n| Flag | Problems that need a redesign, or where the right fix depends on facts outside the document | Don\\'t change the document. Describe the problem and what a redesign must address |\\n\\nFlag rather than fix when proposed changes would touch most of the steps; patching that much\\nleaves a document that is harder to review than a rewrite.\\n\\nDon\\'t weaken an existing control to make the document pass, and don\\'t remove a parameter the\\ndocument needs; change how it is used instead.\\n\\n## Phase 4: Report\\n\\nWrite the report with the structure in\\n[references/automation/hardening-report-template.md](references/automation/hardening-report-template.md): a summary table by severity,\\napplied fixes, proposed fixes as BEFORE / AFTER with their source, flagged items, checks with no\\nfindings, what the review didn\\'t cover, and the complete hardened document in the input\\'s format.\\n\\n## Phase 5: Check the output\\n\\nBefore presenting the report, confirm:\\n\\n- The hardened document parses as YAML or JSON, and every `allowedPattern` in it is still a\\n  valid regular expression.\\n- Every finding names a check from the detection rules and its source page.\\n- No secret value from the input appears anywhere in the report or the hardened document.\\n- Every difference between the input and the hardened document is listed as an applied or\\n  proposed fix.\\n\\nFix anything that doesn\\'t hold before you answer.\\n\\n## Gotchas\\n\\n- Steps inside an `aws:loop` (`inputs.Steps`) are steps too; scan them.\\n- A parameter name containing \"key\" is often an identifier (`KeyName`, `KmsKeyId`, `S3Key`), not a\\n  secret.\\n- `allowedPattern` protects parameters only. A value from `{{StepName.OutputName}}` is never\\n  validated by it.\\n- Patterns must work in both Java regex and Go `regexp`: avoid lookahead and backreferences.\\n- In JSON documents every backslash in a pattern is doubled; in YAML, single-quote the pattern.\\n\\n## Constraints\\n\\n- Report only findings backed by a check in the detection rules.\\n- Never print a secret\\'s value.\\n- Keep the document\\'s behaviour, apart from the fixes you list.\\n- The hardened document must still parse: in JSON, escape backslashes in regular expressions\\n  (`\\\\` becomes `\\\\\\\\`); in YAML, single-quote patterns that contain `\\\\`, `{` or `}`.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_g9jFN0V0G1kIXPpccr13p0", "content": "[{'text': '# Detection rules\\n\\nEach check names the public documentation it relies on. Page names used below:\\n\\n| Short name | Page |\\n|---|---|\\n| Parameters | [Data elements and parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/documents-syntax-data-elements-parameters.html) |\\n| Schemas | [Schemas, features, and examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/documents-schemas-features.html) |\\n| Sharing | [Sharing SSM documents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/documents-ssm-sharing.html) |\\n| Actions | [Systems Manager Automation actions reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-actions.html), section \"Properties shared by all actions\" |\\n| Resource types | [Using inputs from other AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/populating-input-parameters.html) |\\n| Running | [Running an automation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-working-executing.html) |\\n| Script considerations | [Considerations for scripts in runbooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-document-script-considerations.html) |\\n| Parameter Store in Run Command | [Using Parameter Store parameters in Run Command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/sysman-param-runcommand.html) |\\n| Security best practices | [Security best practices for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html) |\\n| Data protection | [Data protection in Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/data-protection.html) |\\n| ARNs | [IAM identifiers: ARN format](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference-arns.html) |\\n| External ID | [Access to AWS accounts owned by third parties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html) |\\n\\nAction pages are linked where used.\\n\\n## 1. Command injection (Critical)\\n\\nCommands run in `aws:runCommand` steps (through `AWS-RunShellScript`, `AWS-RunPowerShellScript` or\\nanother Command document) and in `aws:executeScript` scripts that start processes.\\n\\nFind:\\n\\n1. Every `{{ParameterName}}` inside `aws:runCommand` \u2192 `inputs.Parameters.commands`, or inside any\\n   other input of a Command document that ends up in a command line.\\n2. ## Applied fixes
These are deterministic changes to existing fields.
- **`LogPath`, check 3 (Critical):** `allowedPattern: '.*'` accepts anything, including an empty string. An empty value makes `rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*` run as `rm -rf /*`. I replaced the pattern with a strict path allow-list (see the hardened document). Source: Parameters, Schemas.
- **`InstanceId`, check 3 (High):** it had no `allowedPattern`. I added `^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$`. Source: Parameters.
- **`CheckHealth`, check 5 (Medium):** `timeoutSeconds: 1200` is above the 600-second maximum for `aws:executeScript`. I lowered it to 600. Source: the executeScript action page.
- **`DbPassword`, check 10 (Low):** `SecureString` isn't a valid document parameter type. I changed it to a `String` that holds a Parameter Store parameter name (see the secrets fix below). Source: Parameters.

## Proposed fixes
These change behaviour, so please review each one.

**PROPOSED FIX 1: Constrain and quote `LogPath` (check 1, Critical)**
- **ISSUE:** `{{LogPath}}` is substituted into shell text twice, unquoted, in a command that runs `rm -rf`. Automation substitutes the value before the shell sees it, so any `;`, `$()`, backtick, or `..` in the value runs on the instance.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
  ```
  The pattern is the main control. Quoting is only defense in depth, because a `'` in the value would break out of the quotes, and the pattern excludes quotes.
- **ASSUMPTION:** I limited paths to `/var/log/...` and excluded `..` segments. If your logs live elsewhere, change the prefix, but keep it narrow. Lookahead isn't allowed because the pattern has to work in both Java regex and Go `regexp`.
- **SOURCE:** Schemas ("Parameter security best practices"), Parameters.

**PROPOSED FIX 2: Remove the password from command text (check 2, Critical)**
- **ISSUE:** `echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"` writes the plaintext password into the command document. It then shows up in the Run Command invocation, command output, and execution history. A parameter value is also free-form text, which the Data protection page says shouldn't hold sensitive data.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  - echo "restarting application service"
  ```
  The parameter is now `DbPasswordParameterName`, the name of a Parameter Store `SecureString`. The password is never in the runbook. When you add a real restart command that needs it, read it on the instance:
  ```bash
  DB_PASSWORD=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name '{{DbPasswordParameterName}}' --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text)
  printf '%s' "$DB_PASSWORD" | your-tool --password-stdin
  unset DB_PASSWORD
  ```
  The instance profile then needs `ssm:GetParameter` on that parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on its key. If a real password was ever passed to this runbook, rotate it.
- **SOURCE:** Data protection, Security best practices, Parameter Store in Run Command.

**PROPOSED FIX 3: Remove the hard-coded role (check 4, High)**
- **ISSUE:** `assumeRole` is fixed to `[redacted ARN]`. Other teams, especially in other accounts, can't use the runbook without editing it. It also forces everyone onto one role.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: [redacted ARN]
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
  ```
  This comes with a new `AutomationAssumeRole` parameter of type `AWS::IAM::Role::Arn`. `CheckHealth` calls AWS APIs, so it needs a role.
- **SOURCE:** Script considerations, Running.

**PROPOSED FIX 4: Stop skipping TLS verification (check 9, High)**
- **ISSUE:** `curl -k` accepts any certificate, so the notify call can be intercepted or spoofed.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  - curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  - curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  ```
  If this fails on certificate trust, install your internal CA on the instances or fix the endpoint's certificate. Don't re-add `-k`.
- **SOURCE:** Data protection.

**PROPOSED FIX 5: Fix the `onCancel` target (check 6, Medium)**
- **ISSUE:** `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an `aws:sleep` step. `aws:sleep` can't be an `onCancel` target, so the runbook is invalid or misbehaves when cancelled.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  onCancel: step:Wait
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  onCancel: Abort
  ```
  Nothing in `CheckHealth` needs cleanup on cancel, so a plain abort is the safe choice.
- **SOURCE:** the Actions reference, "Properties shared by all actions".

**For your information, not a finding:** `RotateLogs` has `onFailure: Continue`. If the tar fails, the `&&` stops the delete, but the runbook still carries on to the health check. Confirm that's what you want.

- **7:** there are no approval steps.
- **8:** no step assumes a cross-account role.

- Any Command document the runbook calls beyond how parameters are passed. `AWS-RunShellScript` is AWS-owned.

- **`CheckHealth`, check 5 (Medium):** `timeoutSeconds: 1200` is above the 600-second maximum for `aws:executeScript`. I lowered it to 600. Source: the executeScript action page.
- **`DbPassword`, check 10 (Low):** `SecureString` isn't a valid document parameter type. I changed it to a `String` that holds a Parameter Store parameter name (see the secrets fix below). Source: Parameters.

## Proposed fixes
These change behaviour, so please review each one.

**PROPOSED FIX 1: Constrain and quote `LogPath` (check 1, Critical)**
- **ISSUE:** `{{LogPath}}` is substituted into shell text twice, unquoted, in a command that runs `rm -rf`. Automation substitutes the value before the shell sees it, so any `;`, `$()`, backtick, or `..` in the value runs on the instance.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
  ```
  The pattern is the main control. Quoting is only defense in depth, because a `'` in the value would break out of the quotes, and the pattern excludes quotes.
- **ASSUMPTION:** I limited paths to `/var/log/...` and excluded `..` segments. If your logs live elsewhere, change the prefix, but keep it narrow. Lookahead isn't allowed because the pattern has to work in both Java regex and Go `regexp`.
- **SOURCE:** Schemas ("Parameter security best practices"), Parameters.

**PROPOSED FIX 2: Remove the password from command text (check 2, Critical)**
- **ISSUE:** `echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"` writes the plaintext password into the command document. It then shows up in the Run Command invocation, command output, and execution history. A parameter value is also free-form text, which the Data protection page says shouldn't hold sensitive data.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  - echo "restarting application service"
  ```
  The parameter is now `DbPasswordParameterName`, the name of a Parameter Store `SecureString`. The password is never in the runbook. When you add a real restart command that needs it, read it on the instance:
  ```bash
  DB_PASSWORD=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name '{{DbPasswordParameterName}}' --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text)
  printf '%s' "$DB_PASSWORD" | your-tool --password-stdin
  unset DB_PASSWORD
  ```
  The instance profile then needs `ssm:GetParameter` on that parameter and `kms:Decrypt` on its key. If a real password was ever passed to this runbook, rotate it.
- **SOURCE:** Data protection, Security best practices, Parameter Store in Run Command.

**PROPOSED FIX 3: Remove the hard-coded role (check 4, High)**
- **ISSUE:** `assumeRole` is fixed to `[redacted ARN]`. Other teams, especially in other accounts, can't use the runbook without editing it. It also forces everyone onto one role.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: [redacted ARN]
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
  ```
  This comes with a new `AutomationAssumeRole` parameter of type `AWS::IAM::Role::Arn`. `CheckHealth` calls AWS APIs, so it needs a role.
- **SOURCE:** Script considerations, Running.

**PROPOSED FIX 4: Stop skipping TLS verification (check 9, High)**
- **ISSUE:** `curl -k` accepts any certificate, so the notify call can be intercepted or spoofed.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  - curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  - curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  ```
  If this fails on certificate trust, install your internal CA on the instances or fix the endpoint's certificate. Don't re-add `-k`.
- **SOURCE:** Data protection.

**PROPOSED FIX 5: Fix the `onCancel` target (check 6, Medium)**
- **ISSUE:** `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an `aws:sleep` step. `aws:sleep` can't be an `onCancel` target, so the runbook is invalid or misbehaves when cancelled.
- **BEFORE:**
  ```yaml
  onCancel: step:Wait
  ```
- **AFTER:**
  ```yaml
  onCancel: Abort
  ```
  Nothing in `CheckHealth` needs cleanup on cancel, so a plain abort is the safe choice.
- **SOURCE:** the Actions reference, "Properties shared by all actions".

**For your information, not a finding:** `RotateLogs` has `onFailure: Continue`. If the tar fails, the `&&` stops the delete, but the runbook still carries on to the health check. Confirm that's what you want.

## Not covered by this review
- The IAM policy of the assume role. Review the role separately, especially what a shared role could do on other teams' instances.
- Any Command document the runbook calls beyond how parameters are passed. `AWS-RunShellScript` is AWS-owned.

I also noticed some functional issues that aren't security checks, so I left them unchanged:
- The description says it restarts the service, but no step does.
- `CheckHealth` ignores `InstanceId`. It calls `describe_instance_status()` for every instance in the Region and returns that to anyone who can read the execution output.
- The EC2 response includes datetime values, which may fail serialization.

description: Restarts the app service and rotates its log directory.
assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
    description: (Required) ARN of the role that Automation assumes to run this runbook.
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    description: (Required) ID of the instance to run on.
    allowedPattern: '^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$'

    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)*$'
    maxChars: 255
  DbPasswordParameterName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Name of the SecureString parameter that holds the database password.
    allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]{1,1011}$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Continue
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz '{{LogPath}}' && rm -rf '{{LogPath}}'/*
          - echo "restarting application service"
          - curl https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    onCancel: Abort
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11

        def handler(events, context):
            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}
